mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that distinct AccessAttempts must hold distinct AuditEntries. The injected violation forces two different AccessAttempts to share the same AuditEntry, simulating an in-place mutation (an 'updated' audit record). Both AppendOnly and FR_010_AuditImmutability assert that no two attempts share an entry, so they find a counterexample immediately.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj a1, a2: AccessAttempt | some a1.aAudit and a1.aAudit = a2.aAudit }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that Permitted outcomes require an active CareTeamMembership. The injected violation forces a Permitted RecordsLookup attempt to exist for a caller who has no active membership for the target patient, directly violating the care-team-only authorisation rule from FR-006.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamViolation { some a: AccessAttempt | a.aKind = RecordsLookup and a.aOutcome = Permitted and (no m: CareTeamMembership | m.member = a.aCaller and m.carePatient = a.aTarget and m.mstatus = Active) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the outcome-to-response-shape mapping. The injected violation forces a Denied attempt to return OkShape, making the externally visible response distinguish 'denied' from 'not-found' and leaking the existence of the patient. Both NoInformationLeakage and FR_007_ByteEquivalentDenied catch this.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeakageViolation { some a: AccessAttempt | a.aOutcome = Denied and a.aResponse = OkShape }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the guarantee that every RecordsLookup attempt produces exactly one audit entry. The injected violation forces a RecordsLookup attempt to exist with no linked AuditEntry, simulating the 'record observed without audit trail' scenario that FR-013 and SC-002 prohibit.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMissing { some a: AccessAttempt | a.aKind = RecordsLookup and no a.aAudit }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the enforcement that callers may only invoke operations in their allowed permission matrix cell. The injected violation places an AuditOfficer on a RecordsLookup attempt, which is explicitly denied in the permission matrix and would allow an IG officer to read clinical records directly — violating LeastPrivilege.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PrivilegeViolation { some a: AccessAttempt | a.aCaller.role = AuditOfficer and a.aKind = RecordsLookup }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that an audit entry's recorded clinician and snapshot role must match the AccessAttempt's actual caller. The injected violation forces an audit entry to name a different clinician than the one who made the request — a misattribution that would make the audit log forensically unreliable and violate FR-009's snapshot semantics.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some a: AccessAttempt | some ae: AuditEntry | a.aAudit = ae and ae.aClinician != a.aCaller }
